gaps.why_now: The freeze map needed explicit governance and stay-in-C policy language before a parity scorecard could tell reviewers how a frozen anchor changes status.
The review checklist now asks whether a freeze-map anchor change includes or updates a parity scorecard entry, which keeps Phase 15 governance visible in normal review flow.

Phase 15 needed a reviewable scorecard that records council inputs, evidence thresholds, validation gates, rollback ownership, and the evidence-archive reporting block for every active freeze-in-C anchor.

The Architecture Council review process now requires one decision record with the lane owner, evidence archive path, rollback owner, and latest blocker disposition before a frozen anchor can enter active status review.
The manifest keeps the four deep-core anchors and their governance requirements machine-checkable instead of leaving them as prose only.
A dedicated Phase 15 test gate is the smallest honest way to enforce that every freeze-map anchor carries current governance evidence without inventing implementation progress.
A shared Phase 15 build step keeps the scorecard replayable as a bounded governance lane.
A make target keeps the Phase 15 scorecard runnable with the same discipline as other bounded tranche lanes.
The scorecard now reserves one per-anchor evidence-archive report with a decision record path, linked evidence, benchmark-notes status, replay command, and latest blocker disposition.

The coverage summary now counts anchors with explicit latest blocker dispositions so the maintenance-mode packet can show that every frozen anchor still carries a concrete blocked status instead of relying only on per-anchor prose.
The scorecard now ships reserved per-anchor decision-record templates under the evidence-archive paths so packet headings exist without implying Architecture Council approval.
The scorecard test now keeps the shared review-process packet fields and the per-anchor template headings aligned so governance wording cannot drift silently.
The roadmap expects explicit ownership discipline for active commit series, so each frozen anchor now records the lane owner responsible for keeping its blocked evidence packet current.
The scorecard now records the retained `retired_from_active_discussion` closeout state and the reopen triggers that keep a stay-in-C outcome reviewable without implying approval.
The scorecard now names the bounded reopen-trigger catalog so its retained stay-in-C closeout language stays aligned with the review-process note and evidence-archive packets.

The maintenance-mode handoff now keeps the roadmap source, the bootstrap ledger anchor, and the parked next step visible together so later runs can see why the Phase 15 governance bundle stays landed without reopening deep-core scope.

The top-level docs index needed an explicit Phase 15 governance pointer so reviewers can open the freeze map, review-process note, parity scorecard, indefinite-C policy, evidence-archive templates, and shared phase15 replay path without hunting across unrelated phase notes.
The shared bootstrap replay is already landed, so the scorecard now records the maintenance-mode handoff explicitly instead of carrying a stale shared-CI follow-up name.

The scorecard-side review gate and reserved evidence-archive templates now prove the same current-roadmap-phase, automatic-return-to-blocked, rollback threshold, indefinite-C-policy, and written-rationale fields that the Architecture Council review-process packet already requires.
